principle: robobus seals a message ONCE at its origin (C AES-256-GCM RBX1 ~13 ns => ~77M/s ceiling), relays it as OPAQUE sealed bytes across one or more transports (NO re-encryption per hop , a transport/relay like SHM just moves the already-sealed frame), and opens it ONCE at the sink. So each route reports TWO honest rates: sealed_relay_fps (measured , how fast the transport moves already-sealed frames) and new_sealed_message_fps (producing brand-new sealed messages through it = seal-once + relay, single-core; where the harness seals inline, e.g. kafka native, that measured value IS this). The full TIER LADDER (stock client -> librbxport shim -> native C broker -> raw ceiling) and every compliance profile are attached. All machine-measured; an unoptimized row carries its optimized answer. Profiles share the same AES-256-GCM symmetric leg and differ in the one-time handshake + security level + COMSEC guarantee.
